name: Batch Processing
question: Can this wait a few hours for half the price?
summary: Submit large sets of non-urgent requests as one asynchronous batch. Major providers price batch jobs at about half the standard rate and return results within 24 hours, often much sooner. Ideal for evaluations, classification, enrichment and summaries over large datasets.
useCases: Nightly or weekly jobs nobody waits on
Tagging, extraction or summarization over large archives

items.detail: about 50% off standard pricing on major providers
a file of requests, each with a custom ID
can combine with prompt caching for further savings

steps: Find workloads nobody waits on: nightly jobs, evals, backfills
Write requests to a JSONL file with a custom ID per item
Submit, poll for completion, and match results back by ID
Retry only the failed items in a follow-up batch
pitfalls: No streaming and no real-time answers
Partial failures must be tracked by ID
Very large jobs hit size and rate limits, so split them
remember: Not urgent? Batch it and pay half.
caption: Check your provider’s current batch pricing and limits.

code.text: # Bill check: batch requests are billed at 50% of standard rates

steps.title: Find work nobody waits on
steps.text: Nightly tagging and eval suites fit; live chat and agent loops that need each answer immediately do not.

steps.title: Write one request per line
steps.text: Each line of the JSONL file is a complete request with a unique custom_id, so results can be matched later.

steps.title: Upload, submit and poll
steps.text: Create the batch with a 24-hour completion window, then poll every few minutes. Many batches finish much sooner.

steps.title: Match results by ID
steps.text: Results are not guaranteed to come back in input order. Join each one to its ticket by custom_id.

steps.title: Retry only what failed
steps.text: The error file lists the failed IDs. Resubmit just those in a small follow-up batch, never the whole job.

steps.title: Check the bill
steps.text: 100,000 tickets at $0.0075 each cost $750 through the real-time API and $375 as a batch.

No rate-limit juggling: the provider schedules the work
Simple format: one file of requests with IDs
Stacks with prompt caching and small models
cons: No streaming and no immediate answers
Completion is guaranteed only within the window, often 24 hours

Batch size limits force large jobs to be split

Each result decides the next request, as in an agent loop

library.name: Anthropic Message Batches API
library.what: Submit up to thousands of requests in one call, poll for completion, and read results by custom ID.

numericDrill.question: 10,000 requests, each 1,500 input and 200 output tokens. Standard prices: $3/M input, $15/M output. What's the batch cost at 50% off, in $?
numericDrill.answer: Standard: 15M input × $3 = $45, plus 2M output × $15 = $30, total $75. Batch: $37.50.

interview.question: Which workloads fit batch APIs, and which don't?
interview.answer: Fit: anything nobody waits on, such as nightly tagging, evals, backfills and bulk summaries. Don't fit: interactive chat, agent loops that need each result before the next step, or jobs due within a few hours.

interview.question: How do you handle partial failures in a batch?
interview.answer: Give every request a unique custom ID, record status per ID when results arrive, and resubmit only failed or expired IDs in a follow-up batch, with idempotent writes on your side.

mistakes.mistake: Running nightly jobs through the real-time API
mistakes.fix: Send anything nobody waits on through the batch API

mistakes.mistake: Losing track of which item failed
mistakes.fix: Custom IDs and per-item status tracking

quiz.question: A bank tags 200,000 support tickets every night for a dashboard read the next morning. What is the cheapest suitable approach?
options: The real-time API on a large model
quiz.explanation: Nobody waits on it, so a batch API at about half price is the natural fit.

quiz.question: 20,000 requests each use 2,000 input and 300 output tokens, at $3 and $15 per million. What does the job cost as a batch at 50% off?
quiz.explanation: Input: 40M × $3 = $120. Output: 6M × $15 = $90. Standard $210; batch $105.

quiz.question: Which jobs are good fits for a batch API? Select all that apply.
options: Backfilling sentiment for last year’s reviews
quiz.explanation: Batch suits large independent jobs nobody is waiting on. A live question needs an immediate answer.

quiz.question: Batch results for 30,000 claim notes came back in a different order from the input file. How do you pair them with notes?
quiz.explanation: Results can arrive in any order, so each request carries a custom_id to match it back.

quiz.question: A 50,000-request batch finished with 2% failed. How many requests go into the follow-up batch?
quiz.explanation: 2% of 50,000 = 1,000 failed IDs. Resubmit only those.

quiz.question: Each request has 1,000 shared input tokens read from cache at 0.1×, 500 unique input tokens and 100 output tokens. Prices are $3 and $15 per million, and the batch discount is 50%. What does one request cost?
A churn report is needed within one hour. Is a batch API a safe choice?
options: Yes: batches always finish within an hour
Yes, if the file is small
No: completion is only guaranteed within the batch window, often 24 hours
Only if you poll every minute
quiz.explanation: Many batches finish quickly, but only the window is promised. Tight deadlines need the real-time API.

quiz.question: Which make a workload a poor fit for a batch API? Select all that apply.
options: A user is waiting for the answer
Each result decides the next request
The deadline is shorter than the completion window
quiz.explanation: Batch needs independent requests and time to wait. Large independent jobs are exactly what it is for.

quiz.question: Two million support tickets already sit in a BigQuery table. Which batch option fits best?
quiz.explanation: Vertex AI batch prediction reads from and writes to BigQuery directly.

quiz.question: You run Claude and want up to 100,000 requests in one asynchronous job at half price. Which do you use?
quiz.explanation: The Message Batches API accepts up to 100,000 requests per batch at 50% of standard prices.

quiz.question: A job has 250,000 requests and the provider allows 100,000 per batch. How many batches do you submit?
quiz.explanation: 250,000 ÷ 100,000 = 2.5, rounded up to 3 batches.

quiz.question: What should you track for every request in a batch? Select all that apply.
options: Its status: succeeded, errored or expired
Its position in the input file
quiz.explanation: ID, status and destination make retries and audits reliable. Position is not reliable because order is not guaranteed.

quiz.question: Summarizing 12,000 contracts costs $0.02 each through the real-time API. How much does a batch at 50% off save?
quiz.explanation: 12,000 × $0.02 = $240 standard; half of that, $120, is saved.

quiz.question: A nightly regression eval runs 8,000 test cases, and results are reviewed the next morning. What is the best way to run it?
options: Real-time, one case at a time
quiz.explanation: Eval suites are a textbook batch workload: independent requests and nobody waiting.

quiz.question: Some requests in a batch expired before processing. What should you do?
options: Move the whole pipeline to real-time for good
Resubmit only the expired IDs in a new batch
quiz.explanation: Track status per ID and retry only what did not complete.

quiz.question: Apart from price, what advantages do batch APIs offer? Select all that apply.
options: Separate, typically higher rate limits for batch work
No need to pace requests yourself
Tokens streamed as they are generated
quiz.explanation: The provider schedules the work within its own limits. Batch results are not streamed.

quiz.question: Through the real-time API, a job of 180,000 requests runs at a rate limit of 1,500 requests a minute. How long does it take?
A 60,000-request grading batch had 600 failures, and the team resubmitted the whole batch. What should they have done?
quiz.explanation: Resubmitting everything pays for 60,000 requests again to fix 600, wiping out the discount.

quiz.question: Which statements about batch APIs are true? Select all that apply.
options: Results can arrive in any order
On some providers the discount stacks with prompt caching
Completion is guaranteed within one hour
quiz.explanation: Batches return complete results in any order, and discounts can stack. Only the completion window, often 24 hours, is guaranteed.

quiz.question: A million eval requests cost $4,000 in real time. You move them to a batch at 50% off and to a model costing a quarter as much per request. What do they cost now?
quiz.explanation: $4,000 × 0.5 × 0.25 = $500. Batching and routing stack.
